sentences.text: Respondent(s Order Sheet 08/09/2025 Heard Mr. Shikhar Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioners, and

Ms.
Soumya Sharma, learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for respondent No.1/State.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that respondent No. 2/complainant, who is the wife of petitioner No. 1 and daughter-in-law of petitioners No.2 and 3, lodged a complaint with the Police Station Mahila Thana, Durg (C.G.).

In her complaint, she stated that her marriage with petitioner No. 1 was solemnized according to Muslim customs on 08.07.2018, after which she resided with her Bahadur Shah vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157946532/
1 husband/petitioner No. 1 in the matrimonial home in Bangalore.

sentences.text: She alleged that she was subjected to ill- treatment by her in-laws and, when she became pregnant, was sent to her father's house and was neither cared for nor taken back to her matrimonial home, which prompted her complaint.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that pursuant to this complaint, the Police at Mahila Thana registered an FIR against the petitioners under Sections 498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) on 07.09.2021, bearing FIR No. 94 of 2021.
Following the completion of the investigation, the Police filed the charge-sheet bearing Final Report No. 37 of 2025, dated 27.07.2025, which was presented before the concerned Court on 28.07.2025.
The learned trial Court, thereafter, took cognizance against the petitioners on the same date.
Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that petitioner No. 1/husband also filed MCRCA No. 237 of 2025, in which this Hon'ble Court, on 10.03.2025, referred the matter for mediation.
The mediation was conducted on 02.04.2025, with both parties in attendance, but ultimately failed.
Pursuant to the Court's directions, petitioner No. 1 deposited Rs. 50,000/- with the Mediation Centre of this Court, which was subsequently withdrawn by respondent No. 2.

He also states that vide order dated 07.04.2025, petitioner No. 1/husband was granted anticipatory bail in MCRCA No.
237 of 2025.
Additionally, respondent No. 2 has filed a maintenance case and, following a compromise in that matter, she is receiving Rs. 3,500/- per month as maintenance from petitioner No. 1.
Notice is directed to be issued to respondent No. 2 by speed post.

Learned State Counsel appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondent No. 1; accordingly,
issuance of notice to respondent No. 1 is dispensed with.
Process fee for respondent No. 2 shall be paid within one week.
Notice is made returnable within four weeks.
Two weeks' time is granted to the learned State counsel as well as respondent No. 2 to file their reply- affidavit.
Thereafter, one week's time is granted to the learned counsel for the petitioners to file a rejoinder- affidavit, if any.
The matter shall be listed thereafter.

Till the next date of listing, the proceedings pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Durg, District Durg (C.G.) in Criminal Case RCC No. 24109 of 2025 against the petitioners shall remain stayed.
